paper_metadata.title: Software for Creating Scalable Benchmarks from Quantum Algorithms

summary: This paper introduces scarab, a tool for turning quantum circuits into scalable process-fidelity benchmarks using mirror-circuit fidelity estimation. It demonstrates low-level Hamiltonian-simulation benchmarks on 2–10 qubits in simulation and 5-qubit IBM Kingston experiments, plus full-stack approximate-compilation benchmarks for QFT and QAOA on IBM Fez, with process fidelity tracked versus approximation degree and Trotter step count.

experiments.description: Low-level Hamiltonian simulation benchmarks for first-order Trotter circuits on TFIM, Heisenberg, Bose-Hubbard, and Fermi-Hubbard Hamiltonians, evaluated in simulation and on IBM Kingston/IBM Fez to estimate noise process fidelity and full process fidelity.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Hamiltonian simulation circuits compiled to IBM native gate set {X, SX, RZ, CZ}; no QUBO/Ising encoding described beyond Hamiltonian-to-circuit synthesis.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Approximate unitary evolution U = exp(-iHt) via first-order Trotterization; benchmark process fidelity of noisy implementation against ideal or noise-free Trotter unitary.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: TFIM, Heisenberg, Bose-Hubbard, and Fermi-Hubbard Hamiltonians from HamLib

problem_instance.description: Benchmarking Hamiltonian simulation circuits for multiple model Hamiltonians and varying qubit counts/time steps.

dataset_specification.description: TFIM, Heisenberg, Bose-Hubbard, and Fermi-Hubbard Hamiltonians from HamLib; 1D lattice settings described in appendix

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Process fidelities estimated with scarab mirror-circuit benchmarks; compared against exact values in simulation and against IBM Kingston/IBM Fez experimental results; bootstrap error bars reported.

hardware.device_name: IBM Kingston simulator / qiskit_aer simulation of IBM Kingston

implementation_details.transpilation_target: IBM native gate set {X, SX, RZ, CZ}
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Hamiltonians selected from HamLib; Trotter circuits generated from Hamiltonians.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: scarab data analysis to estimate process fidelities; bootstrap uncertainty estimation.

speedup_claims.factor: linear scaling vs exponentially growing classical simulation
speedup_claims.baseline_method: qiskit_aer classical simulation of the same circuits
speedup_claims.conditions: for low-level and subcircuit benchmarks up to n=10000; full-stack benchmark up to n=150 on IBM Fez
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports runtime scaling of the classical processing in scarab, not a formal asymptotic speedup proof for quantum computation.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No advantage claim; benchmark compares process fidelity of Trotterized Hamiltonian simulation circuits under noise and approximation.
limiting_factors: Objective is fidelity estimation, not computational speedup

notes: Hardware type inferred as simulator_noisy for the simulation runs because the paper explicitly states qiskit_aer simulation of IBM Kingston; experimental runs on IBM Kingston/IBM Fez are also described in the same experiment family.
No explicit asymptotic speedup claim is made for these benchmarks.
The paper reports benchmark fidelity estimates for Hamiltonian simulation circuits in simulation and experiment, but does not claim quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Experimental Hamiltonian simulation benchmarks on IBM Kingston for 5-qubit Heisenberg and Max3SAT Hamiltonians using first- and second-order Trotterization with varying time steps, estimating noise and full process fidelity.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Hamiltonian simulation circuits compiled to IBM native gate set; Max3SAT represented as a Hamiltonian sum of clause terms.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Approximate ideal Hamiltonian evolution and quantify tradeoff between Trotter approximation error and hardware noise via process fidelity.

problem_instance.description: 5-qubit Hamiltonian simulation on IBM Kingston with varying Trotter step counts.

dataset_specification.description: 5-qubit Heisenberg and Max3SAT Hamiltonians; Max3SAT instance flag rinst=02 in appendix

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Benchmarks run on IBM Kingston and IBM Fez simulator; full process fidelity estimated from measured noise process fidelity and exact algorithmic process fidelity; bootstrap error bars reported.

noise_model.noise_type: hardware noise on IBM Kingston; simulator comparison also used

implementation_details.transpilation_target: IBM native gate set {X, SX, RZ, CZ}
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Trotter circuit generation from Hamiltonians; exact algorithmic fidelities computed in simulation.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: scarab estimation of noise process fidelity and product-form estimate of full process fidelity.

speedup_claims.caveats: This is a benchmarking study; no speedup claim is made.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No advantage claim; the experiment studies tradeoffs between Trotter order, time steps, and hardware noise on a 5-qubit device.
limiting_factors: No classical baseline for solving the underlying problem
Metric is process fidelity, not task advantage

notes: The paper explicitly states 5-qubit Heisenberg and Max3SAT Hamiltonians and varying time steps, but does not give a total circuit depth number.
No asymptotic speedup analysis is provided.
The paper reports IBM Kingston experiments and simulator comparisons, but no advantage claim or classical baseline.

experiments.description: Full-stack benchmark of approximate compilation for QFT circuits on IBM Fez and its simulator, measuring process fidelity versus approximation degree and compiled depth.

algorithm.variant: QFT full-stack benchmark for approximate compilation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: QFT circuits used as algorithmic benchmarks; no explicit problem encoding beyond the circuit itself.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Measure process fidelity of compiled QFT circuits to the ideal approximation-free unitaries.

problem_instance.description: QFT circuits of varying size used to test approximate compilation.

dataset_specification.description: n-qubit QFT circuits for n=2 to 10

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 10 transpilations of each high-level circuit; process fidelity estimated with scarab on IBM Fez and qiskit_aer simulation of IBM Fez.

noise_model.noise_type: IBM Fez hardware noise and IBM Fez noise-model simulation

implementation_details.transpilation_target: IBM Fez native compilation via qiskit transpiler
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: QFT circuits generated from qiskit library; approximate compilation applied.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: scarab process fidelity estimation and bootstrap confidence intervals.

speedup_claims.caveats: No speedup claim; the experiment evaluates approximate compilation quality and depth.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No advantage claim; the experiment evaluates approximate compilation quality for QFT circuits on IBM Fez and its simulator.
limiting_factors: No classical baseline for a computational task
Benchmark measures process fidelity and circuit depth, not end-to-end application performance
QFT is used as a circuit family, not as a demonstrated advantage workload

notes: The paper reports n=2 to n=10 QFT circuits and compiled depths are shown in a figure, but exact depth values are not enumerated in text.
No speedup claim is made; this is a benchmarking study.
The paper reports process fidelity versus approximation degree for QFT compilation, but does not claim quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Full-stack benchmark of approximate compilation for QAOA circuits on IBM Fez and its simulator, measuring process fidelity versus approximation degree and compiled depth.

algorithm.variant: QAOA full-stack benchmark for approximate compilation
algorithm.parameter_initialization: mixing angles initialized uniformly between 0 and π

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Random graph optimization problem encoded as a QAOA cost Hamiltonian; one qubit per binary variable implied by QAOA graph formulation.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Optimize the QAOA cost Hamiltonian for a random GNP(n, 2 ln(n)/n) graph.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: QAOA cost Hamiltonian for random GNP(n, 2 ln(n)/n) graph

problem_instance.description: QAOA circuits on random graphs of size n=2 to 10 used to test approximate compilation.

dataset_specification.description: GNP(n, 2 ln(n)/n) graphs; one repetition of each operator

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 10 transpilations of each high-level circuit; process fidelity estimated with scarab on IBM Fez and qiskit_aer simulation of IBM Fez.

noise_model.noise_type: IBM Fez hardware noise and IBM Fez noise-model simulation

implementation_details.transpilation_target: IBM Fez native compilation via qiskit transpiler
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Random graph generation and QAOA circuit construction from qiskit library.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: scarab process fidelity estimation and bootstrap confidence intervals.

speedup_claims.caveats: No speedup claim; this is a compiler-benchmarking study.

notes: The paper states one repetition of each operator and varying approximation degree, but does not explicitly state the QAOA layer count p; p=1 is inferred from one repetition.
No asymptotic speedup claim is made; this is a compiler-benchmarking study.

experiments.description: Subcircuit benchmarking of a 6-qubit QFT and scalable low-level benchmarking of QFT(n) for n=2..6 on IBM Kingston and its simulator, used to predict full-circuit fidelity from subcircuits and varying-size circuits.

algorithm.variant: QFT subcircuit benchmark and varying-size QFT benchmark

problem_formulation.encoding_details: QFT circuits used as benchmark circuits; subcircuits sampled from a compiled 6-qubit QFT and from QFT(n) circuits.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate process fidelity of subcircuits and use them to predict full-circuit fidelity.

problem_instance.description: 6-qubit QFT subcircuit benchmark plus varying-size QFT benchmarks for n=2..6.

dataset_specification.description: Compiled 6-qubit QFT on IBM Kingston; QFT(n) for n=2,3,4,5,6

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Run on IBM Kingston and qiskit_aer simulation of IBM Kingston; 30 subcircuits per shape; compare measured process fidelities and predictions from effective error rates/GPR.

noise_model.noise_type: IBM Kingston hardware noise and IBM Kingston simulator

implementation_details.transpilation_target: IBM Kingston native compilation via qiskit transpiler
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compiled QFT circuits used to generate subcircuits; Gaussian process regression and effective error rate modeling used for prediction.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: scarab process fidelity estimation, effective error rate calculation, and GPR-based prediction.

speedup_claims.caveats: No speedup claim; the experiment studies prediction of full-circuit fidelity from subcircuits.

notes: The paper explicitly reports subcircuit shapes with depths 21, 23, 25, and 27 and QFT sizes n=2..6.
No speedup claim is made; this is a benchmarking/prediction study.

experiments.description: Full-stack benchmark of approximate compilation for QAOA circuits on IBM Fez and qiskit_aer simulation of IBM Fez, measuring process fidelity versus approximation degree and compiled depth.

algorithm.variant: QAOA full-stack benchmark for approximate compilation

key_results: Process fidelity was evaluated for compiled QAOA circuits on IBM Fez and a qiskit_aer simulation of IBM Fez.
In most cases, approximation_degree = 1.0 gave the largest or near-largest process fidelity.
